beats.note: Snopes quotes 1911 coverage saying the closing watertight doors made the vessel practically unsinkable. Wikipedia says three trade publications used the hedge.

beats.text: White Star sold size, not safety.
beats.note: Snopes says its adverts called the ships the largest and finest steamers. It adds that a flyer found in 1993 said they were designed to be unsinkable as far as it is possible to do.

beats.text: The walls did not reach the top.
beats.note: History.com says the bulkheads rose only a few feet above the waterline, so water spilled from one compartment into the next.

beats.context: The lifeboat capacity. History.com puts the number aboard at 2,240.

beats.note: She sank at about 2:20 a.m. on 15 April 1912. History.com says 706 survived.
On 16 April 1912 the New York Times quoted an executive of the owning group: I thought her unsinkable.

beats.text: The hedge vanished. The word stuck.
